paper.title_en: Delivery of refractory radioactive ion beams via in-trap decay at ISOLDE
paper.abstract_en: An approach to deliver intense ion beams of refractory radioactive isotopes utilizing in-trap <math><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></math> decay is demonstrated using the gas-filled ISCOOL ion trap at CERN-ISOLDE. Ion beams of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rb</mi><none/><mo>+</mo><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Sr</mi><none/><mo>+</mo><mprescripts/><none/><mn>98</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were injected into the ion trap, where they underwent <math><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></math> decay and the daughter ions were successfully confined in the same trap. The produced singly charged ions were subsequently extracted and identified using the ISOLTRAP multireflection time-of-flight mass spectrometer, where the beam composition was analyzed as a function of trapping time. Modeling the observed time-dependent populations of the parent and daughter ions using the Bateman equations reproduces the isotopes' known half-lives, thereby confirming production via in-trap decay, achieving an overall efficiency for the singly charged daughter beams on the order of <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></math> relative to the parent intensity. Using this method, delivery of a singly charged atomic ion beam of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><none/><mo>+</mo><mprescripts/><none/><mn>98</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is thus reported for the first time at ISOLDE. These results demonstrate a practical and operationally simple method for delivering refractory isotopes at thick-target isotope-separation-on-line facilities, opening new opportunities for nuclear-structure studies of chemically challenging isotopes.
